bio.short: I'm Hardik, a product engineer in Ahmedabad. I take products from the first sketch to a production release: interface design, web and mobile apps, and the AI features inside them.
bio.medium: I'm Hardik, a product engineer in Ahmedabad, India. Over the last four years I have built ordering platforms, clinic tools, desktop and Android apps for startups and growing businesses. I design the interface, write the code and stay accountable for the result. AI coding agents work alongside me on the routine parts, which is why projects move at the pace of a small team.

principles.title: Small-team speed, one point of contact
principles.body: AI coding agents handle routine implementation while I design, review and own every change. You get the output of a small team and talk to one person.

principles.title: Design and code in one head
principles.body: The person who designs the screen also builds it, so nothing gets lost between a mockup and the release.

principles.title: Built to stay easy to change
principles.body: Typed code, automated tests and reviewed releases from day one, so the product keeps moving after launch.

projects.title: Wholesale OS
projects.oneLiner: One system for orders, stock and invoices, replacing spreadsheets and phone calls.
projects.challenge: Sales reps took orders on paper and over the phone, and stock and invoices lived in separate spreadsheets.
projects.approach: A multi-tenant web platform with offline order capture for reps on the road, live stock, and invoicing in one place.
projects.outcome: Orders taken offline sync on their own, and the office works from one source of truth.
projects.visual: Desktop dashboard: sidebar nav, order table with status pills, stock level bars, an invoice drawer.

projects.title: MedJot
projects.oneLiner: A clinic notebook that lets a doctor record a visit faster than on paper, even offline.
projects.challenge: Small clinics still rely on paper registers because clinic software is slow, online-only and built for hospitals.
projects.approach: A mobile-first installable app that keeps all data on the device, with symptom chips, learned autocomplete and a command palette.
projects.outcome: A full visit, from symptoms to a printed receipt, takes a few taps.
projects.visual: Phone screens: patient visit form with symptom chips, medicine autocomplete list, a receipt preview.

projects.title: Paper Studio
projects.oneLiner: Builds print-ready exam papers from a question bank, with AI drafting the first version.
projects.challenge: Teachers spent evenings formatting papers, answer keys and OMR sheets by hand.
projects.approach: A question bank with versioned questions, AI-drafted papers and instant typesetting in the browser.
projects.outcome: A complete paper with its answer key is ready in minutes instead of hours.
projects.visual: Split view: question list on the left, typeset A4 paper preview on the right, an 'AI draft' button.

projects.title: Fieldbook
projects.oneLiner: A mobile app for field sales reps: catalogue, orders and today's route, online or not.
projects.challenge: Reps visit shops with patchy signal and need prices, stock and order history in their pocket.
projects.approach: A cross-platform iOS and Android app with an offline catalogue, quick reorder and a daily route plan.
projects.outcome: A reorder takes under thirty seconds at the counter.
projects.visual: Three phone screens: today's route list, product catalogue grid, cart with 'Place order'.

projects.title: Footnote
projects.oneLiner: An AI research assistant that answers from your documents and shows exactly where each claim comes from.
projects.challenge: Teams don't trust AI answers they can't verify.
projects.approach: A chat interface that streams answers with inline citations, plus a sources panel that highlights the quoted passage.
projects.outcome: Every sentence links back to its source.
projects.visual: Chat answer with numbered citation chips, right panel showing a document with the cited passage highlighted.

projects.title: Kiln UI
projects.oneLiner: A design system with tokens, 40 accessible components and docs, so teams ship consistent UI faster.
projects.challenge: Growing products end up with five button styles and no shared language between design and code.
projects.approach: Design tokens in Figma and code, a component library tested for accessibility, and a docs site with live examples.
projects.outcome: New screens are assembled, not redrawn.
projects.visual: Token sheet: colour swatches, type scale, spacing ruler, a grid of buttons, inputs and toggles in several states.

projects.title: Dhi
projects.oneLiner: A desktop knowledge base that reads your documents and grows a linked map of ideas.
projects.challenge: Notes pile up in folders and the connections between ideas get lost.
projects.approach: A Tauri desktop app that ingests documents with an LLM, writes linked notes and draws them as an explorable graph.
projects.outcome: Related ideas surface on their own, in a fast native window.
projects.visual: Desktop window: editor on the left, a node-link knowledge graph with coloured clusters on the right.

projects.title: Net Watch
projects.oneLiner: An Android app that records network drops on a timeline you can export.
projects.challenge: "The internet keeps cutting out" is hard to prove to a provider.
projects.approach: A native Kotlin app with a background monitor and a clear timeline of every drop and slow period.
projects.outcome: A shareable report instead of a hunch.
projects.visual: Phone screen: timeline of connection events with red drop markers and an Export button.

faq.a: Fixed price for a scoped project, agreed after a free planning call. Ongoing work is a monthly plan.

faq.q: Do you use AI to write code?
faq.a: Yes. AI agents take on routine implementation, and I design, review and take responsibility for every change. It makes projects faster without lowering the bar.

faq.q: Which time zones do you work with?
faq.a: I'm on IST and overlap with mornings in Europe and evenings in Australia. Updates are written, so nothing waits for a meeting.
You do, from the first commit. Everything lives in your repository and your accounts.

faq.q: Can you work with my existing team?
faq.a: Yes. I can lead a feature end to end or slot into your process and tools.
Thirty days of fixes are included. After that, an ongoing plan covers improvements and new features.
